notes: Session 2. Closed B5-0628, which came from the HUMAN's own failed hermes run rather than from a seeded row, and their terminal output supplied the evidence: hermes rejected the tail of the task prompt with 'is not a hermes command' and exited 2. Reading the error before theorising located the cause, because the fragment hermes quoted began immediately after the phrase 'Reusable lesson' in the template. Root cause: Windows PowerShell 5.1 does NOT escape embedded double quotes when handing an argument to a native executable, so the quotes act as argument delimiters, the prompt splits into several argv entries, the first fragment is consumed as the prompt and the rest are read as positional arguments, and a subcommand-style CLI reports the last as an invalid command. It survived unnoticed because CLIs taking a bare positional prompt are unaffected and the runner had presumably only been pointed at one of those. MY FIRST HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG: I suspected newlines, and a two-line prompt exited 0 and was understood, proving newlines are safe and are NOT the trigger; had the fix been the obvious reflex of collapsing the prompt to one line, the quotes would still have split it and the runner would still have been broken. Four controlled cases against hermes itself before any edit. METHODOLOGICAL NOTE worth keeping: a .ps1 stub was tried first and DELIBERATELY NOT RELIED ON, because a PowerShell script receives .NET objects and never exercises the Windows command-line marshaller, so ARGC=1 from it would have been a false proof; the tell was noticing the stub and the caller were the same kind of thing. A native python.exe argv dumper was used instead, receiving arguments through the identical Windows path as hermes. End to end, running the REAL runner against that dumper: ARGC=1, length 1007, CONTAINS_DOUBLEQUOTE=False, NEWLINE_COUNT=12 preserved, HAS_TASKID=True. Control in the same path with quotes retained: ARGC=2, fragments of 18 and 38 chars, exactly the human's failure. Fix is the minimal one the evidence supports: $safePrompt = $prompt -replace double-quote, single-quote at the single invocation site, with a comment recording the reproduction, and the multi-line structure deliberately preserved because newlines were tested harmless. SIDE EFFECT I CAUSED AND REMOVED, disclosed not glossed: the isolation probe was a live prompt telling hermes to write a reusable-lesson file, and hermes complied, creating .agent/PATTERNS/solar-pro4<U+2028>free/lesson-compile-gate-grep.md inside solar-pro4's namespace, which this agent may read but must never write; confirmed as this session's own creation by its 04:24:28Z creation time against a 02:34Z session start, contents read to confirm, then deleted, leaving all eight pre-existing files there untouched. Lesson: a reproduction against a live tool must use a prompt that cannot cause a side effect, because the tool does exactly what it is told and the discipline belongs to whoever writes the probe. STILL OPEN: -AgentArgs appends a single element so multi-flag strings like '-z --yolo' arrive malformed; fixing it needs either whitespace splitting, which breaks paths with spaces, or a wrapper script, and neither is a one-liner so it is reported not absorbed. All temp harnesses in TEMP removed. Gates green: compile.bat Build successful, runner exit 0, no crash, no duplicate warning. Reusable lesson: when a native call fails in a way that looks like the TOOL misunderstanding your input, suspect the shell's argument marshalling before the tool, and reproduce with a probe that crosses the same boundary, because a stub written in the calling language will happily confirm what the real call does not do.
